impl.summary:
Done. verifyModAssets in build.gradle.kts now refuses a .so that has non-weak undefined dynamic symbols with no version. I verified it with the real task (`./gradlew --offline --no-daemon verifyModAssets -Pocljit.nativesDir=<scratch>`) on 19 new cases and on the glibc round's 34 cases. I edited no other repo file, and nothing under build/native was read as natives or written.

Results [M]:
- **The trial .so (bf0d0916)** is refused, naming the six pthread symbols: pthread_attr_setstacksize, pthread_condattr_setclock, pthread_create, pthread_join, pthread_setname_np and pthread_sigmask. HEAD's build.gradle.kts (md5 67153bd5) accepts the same directory (BUILD SUCCESSFUL), so this is a real fail-first.
- **The release .so (6c888050)** is accepted, alone and together with dist's DLL. Its line now ends "110 imports, every non-weak one versioned (weak and unversioned: _ITM_deregisterTMCloneTable, _ITM_registerTMCloneTable, __gmon_start__)".
- **Every mutant behaved as it should.** HEAD accepts all of them, and the new task refuses each one meant to be refused, with our own message and no exception text.
- **The glibc round's cases are unchanged.** Every line of every case is the same as under HEAD, except two expected changes: c02-trial is now refused, and passing cases have the import count added to their glibc line. Exit codes match runs-final-1 except c02.

Final file: 512 lines, CR 0, md5 942605fcf6ff270a26e9b2a07beee5a5, git diff +105/-8.

Where it runs: the symbol tables are read right after the existing version-needs walk, before any verdict, so a file whose symbols don't parse is refused as unreadable. The unversioned verdict comes after the GLIBC_x.y checks, for two reasons. Every .so the floor refused before is still refused in the same words (measured on the 34 cases). And the floor's fix, building with build-native.sh in AlmaLinux 8, also removes unversioned imports, because build-native.sh's import gate refuses them.

One addition you didn't specify: a version index of 2 or more must match a vna_other value from .gnu.version_r. Otherwise it is refused as a corrupt file. Without this, an index such as 0x7ff0 would count as versioned even though no version record defines it.
findings:
[M] The change, all in verifyModAssets' existing ELF loop:
- name() takes an optional string table, and its messages are unchanged.
- The verneed walk also collects each Vernaux's vna_other into `assigned`.
- A new block (comment :338-364) finds exactly one SHT_DYNSYM. Its sh_entsize must be 24, its size a multiple of 24, and its sh_link an SHT_STRTAB in range.
- At most one SHT_GNU_versym is allowed. When present, its size must be 2 x the symbol count and its sh_link must name .dynsym.
- It counts imports (st_shndx 0 with a non-empty name), masks each version with 0x7fff, sorts index < 2 into weak or unversioned, and refuses an index of 2 or more that no Vernaux assigns.
- It refuses a .dynsym with no imports at all, so the check cannot pass vacuously.
- After the floor refusal it throws for unversioned imports (12 names at most, then 'and N more'). The passing lifecycle line gains '; N imports, every non-weak one versioned (weak and unversioned: ...)'.

[M] Bounded work: one pass over .dynsym (at most file size / 24 entries). Whether a name is empty or properly terminated is judged against the table's last NUL, found once. Names are built only for the capped lists. A crafted file can therefore not make the scan quadratic: a direct name() call per symbol would rescan each string.

[M] New cases, runs-head-u (HEAD) against runs-final-u (final md5 942605fc). HEAD accepted all 19.
- Accepted now: u02 release, u03 release plus DLL, u04 alma-new, u07 (pthread_once, WEAK, versym 3 -> 1: accepted and listed among the weak ones), u14 (pthread_create versym with the hidden bit on a valid index).
- Refused as unversioned: u01 trial (six pthread symbols), u05 (pthread_create versym 1), u06 (versym 0), u15 (0x8001, which masks to 1), u08 (.gnu.version sh_type changed: '104 symbols', which is 110 imports minus 6 weak).
- Refused as unreadable, each with our reason: u09 sh_entsize 16; u10 .gnu.version 748 bytes for 375 symbols; u11 .dynsym sh_link 200; u12 name at offset 9440 outside its table; u13 index 32752 assigned by no Vernaux; u16 .dynsym 8992 bytes; u17 two SHT_DYNSYM; u18 no imports; u19 name runs past the end of its table.

[M] Regression check: scripts/crosscheck.py on the final runs reports 0 problems.
- For all 33 old cases other than c02 (c00-empty and c33-dropin included), every OC-LuaJIT line and every failure reason equals HEAD's (runs-head-old and -old3). The only change is the import suffix on passing glibc lines (c03, c05, c10, c11).
- c02-trial changes from rc 0 to refused, as expected.
- Exit codes equal runs-final-1's for all 32 of its cases, except c02.
- 162 logs were scanned: none contains exception text, and every failure reason is a '> OC-LuaJIT:' or dropin-guard line.
- 'Configuration cache entry stored.' appears in all 53 final logs, with no configuration-cache problems.

[M] The crosscheck was shown to fail: I planted four faults in a copy of the runs (xc-neg/) and it flagged all of them (6 problems). They were an exception line, a changed fingerprint line, a wrong suffix on a glibc line, and the wrong symbol in u05.

[M] readelf --dyn-syms -W agrees on the real files, in AlmaLinux 8 (binutils 2.30) and Ubuntu (binutils 2.46).
- release: 110 UND, weak unversioned are the same three.
- trial: the same six non-weak unversioned names (its weak unversioned also include __pthread_key_create and pthread_once).
- alma-new: 110 and the same weak three.
r3, nolibgcc and libdl have no non-weak unversioned imports. On the mutants, u05, u06 and u15 show pthread_create with no version in both readelf versions.

[M] Two places where readers disagree, both on crafted files only:
- u08: readelf still shows versions, because it finds versym through the dynamic section's DT_VERSYM. The gate reads section headers, so it refuses, which is the safe direction.
- u14 (hidden bit on an import's valid index): the gate accepts it, as the 0x7fff mask you specified implies. readelf 2.30 prints no version and 2.46 prints '@<corrupt>'. [I] glibc's loader masks with 0x7fff when it resolves a relocation (from memory of elf/do-rel.h; I did not read it this session).

[M] c08 (AlmaLinux 8's libdl-2.28.so, which has a .gnu.version_d section) reads cleanly and keeps its old GLIBC_PRIVATE refusal. So a real glibc library that also defines versions does not trip the vna_other check.

verify.summary: ADVERSARIAL VERDICT: I found no defect in the implementer's change to build.gradle.kts (md5 942605fcf6ff270a26e9b2a07beee5a5, unchanged by me). The new .so block correctly refuses a .so with non-weak unversioned dynamic imports, accepts the release .so and the three allowed weak symbols, matches readelf on every real file I could find, has zero false accepts and zero false refuses, and handles crafted/corrupt input with clean GradleExceptions (no uncaught exception, no hang). The two residual items are pre-existing limitations shared with build-native.sh's readelf gate and already noted in the implementer's open_questions; neither is a shipping-defect. I did not edit build.gradle.kts or anything under build/native; every gradle run was the real task against fresh scratch natives dirs.
findings: [M] FIDELITY: a faithful Python reimplementation of the new .so block (verify/scripts/gate.py, same order, Kotlin signed-Long u64) reproduces the REAL gradle task's verdict on all 19 implementer cases (runs-final-u) and on 10 new adversarial cases I ran through the real task (verify/runs-adv): every pass/refuse and every refusal reason matched. So the reimplementation is a trustworthy oracle for the large-scale cross-check below.

[M] NO FALSE ACCEPT: across 3219 real files -- AlmaLinux 8 /usr/lib64+/usr/bin+/usr/sbin+/usr/libexec+/usr/lib/jvm (1558), Ubuntu (1655), OC's own stock libjnlua52-linux-x86_64.so from OC-JNLua-Natives-20220928.1.jar, and the 6 input .so/.dll -- there is not one file the gate would PASS that readelf --dyn-syms -W shows with a non-weak unversioned UND. Checked explicitly: 0 false accepts.

[M] NO FALSE REFUSE: across the same 3219 files there is not one file the gate marks 'unv' that readelf shows as clean (no non-weak unversioned UND). 0 false refuses. OC's stock libjnlua52-linux-x86_64.so (md5 eaca37be) PASSES: 80 imports, only __gmon_start__ weak-unversioned, highest need GLIBC_2.14 -- so the parser accepts a real good .so from a different toolchain. Gate import-set vs readelf import-set: 0 SETS DIFFER on every parseable file.

[M] THE TWO ANCHORS HOLD: release.so (6c888050, = build/native/dist) PASSES alone and with the DLL, reporting '110 imports, every non-weak one versioned (weak and unversioned: _ITM_deregisterTMCloneTable, _ITM_registerTMCloneTable, __gmon_start__)'. trial.so (bf0d0916) is REFUSED naming exactly the six pthread symbols. readelf in both binutils 2.30 (Alma) and the newer Ubuntu agrees on both.

[M] CRASH/HANG PROBES ALL REFUSED CLEANLY (real gradle, verify/runs-adv): dynsym sh_size 0x7fffffffffffffff (a7), versym sh_offset 0x8000000000000000 (a8), e_shnum 65535 with truncated table (a9), first Verneed vn_cnt 65535 (a10), versym index 0x7fff dangling (a5). Each exits rc=1 with a single '> OC-LuaJIT: ... is not an ELF64 shared object this check can read (...)' GradleException -- no stack trace, no 'Exception' text, no hang (each 5-6s). The bounds checks (at(), section(), room, lastNul, read>room) catch every overflow and negative offset; name() cannot read out of bounds because every string table end is clamped to <= file size.

[I/M] THE THREE 'PASS' ADVERSARIAL CASES ARE NOT FALSE ACCEPTS. Setting the six trial imports' st_shndx to SHN_XINDEX 0xffff (a1), SHN_ABS 0xfff1 (a2), or their name offset to 0/empty (a3) makes the gate PASS -- but readelf shows the same symbols as RSV[0xffff], ABS, or empty-named, i.e. NO LONGER undefined imports, and build-native.sh's readelf gate (which keys on column 7 == UND) would also not flag them. The loader likewise treats st_shndx != SHN_UNDEF as a definition. These convert an import into a broken address-0 definition (library LOADS, then crashes when the symbol is called) -- a different failure mode from the 'unversioned import -> fails to load' defect the gate targets, consistent across the gradle gate, the build-time gate and readelf, and emitted by no honest linker. Not a gate-specific miss; worth a one-line mention at most.

[M] VERSYM SEMANTICS CONFIRMED CORRECT against the ELF gABI: index 0 (local) and 1 (global unversioned base) -> treated as unversioned (refused if non-weak); the 0x8000 hidden bit is masked by 0x7fff so 0x8001 -> 1 -> refused (a-equivalent of u15) while 0x8000|valid -> valid -> accepted (matches the loader's VERSYM_VERSION mask); an index >=2 that no Vernaux vna_other assigns -> refused as corrupt (a5, 0x7fff->32767); an index >=2 that IS assigned and names a real need -> treated as versioned (a4, release pthread_create set to versym 2 = GLIBC_2.2.5 passes, which is correct because it is then genuinely versioned). WEAK (bind 2) listed not refused; GNU_UNIQUE (10), LOCAL (0), bind 15 -> all refused as non-weak (safe); st_other visibility HIDDEN/PROTECTED/INTERNAL does not let an import slip (still refused).

open_questions: Section-header vs DT_VERSYM divergence (implementer open_question 3, CONFIRMED as a shared limitation, NOT a defect of this change): the gate finds .gnu.version by section type SHT_GNU_versym, exactly as readelf and build-native.sh's readelf gate do, while the dynamic loader uses the dynamic segment's DT_VERSYM. A deliberately malicious ELF whose section-header versym and dynamic-segment versym disagree could pass both gates yet bind unversioned at load. This is beyond the task's 'stale or mis-linked .so' threat model, is not introduced by this change, and affects the build-time gate identically. Reading PT_DYNAMIC's DT_VERSYM would close it but is not required to fix the stated defect.

Hidden bit 0x8000 on an import's otherwise-valid version index (implementer open_question 1): the gate masks with 0x7fff and accepts, matching glibc's loader (VERSYM_VERSION mask); readelf 2.46 prints '@<corrupt>' and readelf 2.30 prints no version. ld never emits this on an undefined symbol. The gate's choice matches the loader, so accepting is defensible; refusing it as malformed would be stricter but is a judgement call for the owner.

Not a gate concern, flagged only for completeness: a .so with ZERO imports and no .gnu.version_r is refused as 'unreadable' (the floor check's one-.gnu.version_r requirement, which predates this change). No .so in OC-LuaJIT's shippable family is in that shape, so there is no false refuse of a real artifact; the 14 such files in my survey were ld.so/ldconfig/static helpers, already refused by HEAD.
